prompt: Draw the network map of a fictional city's metro, as a single self-contained SVG, in the flat diagrammatic style of a printed transit map rather than a geographic one. At least four routes in distinct colours run across the sheet and cross each other; every segment of every route runs horizontally, vertically or at exactly 45 degrees, and no route comes near another except where they meet at a marked interchange. Each route is punctuated by evenly spaced station ticks, carries a named terminus at both of its ends, and shares its interchanges with the routes that cross it there. A river runs across the sheet and the network bridges it in more than one place. Around the diagram sit the furniture that makes a map readable: a masthead naming the operator, a legend giving a swatch and a name for every route plus the station symbols, a scale bar with a distance in kilometres, and a compass rose labelled N. The whole drawing is vector, inline and offline: no scripts, no raster images, no fonts or assets fetched from anywhere.
definition_of_done: final_output_file: metro-map.svg, a single self-contained SVG. All 14 cases in test_acceptance.py pass via `python -I -m unittest discover -s . -v` with exit code 0. 1. The file parses as XML, the root is <svg>, and its viewBox holds 4 numbers describing a sheet at least 600 wide and 400 tall. 2. Elements carry exactly these ids: map, backdrop, river, river-course, bridges, lines, stations, labels, legend, scale, compass, masthead. 3. The file makes zero external requests: no http(s) href or src, no @import, no url(//...). 4. It contains no <script>, no <image> and no <foreignObject>. 5. At least 4 groups are named route-<letter>; each holds a <polyline class="centreline"> of at least 4 points, and each carries a stroke colour no other route uses. 6. Every centreline segment is octolinear and real: horizontal, vertical, or at 45 degrees within 2 percent, and longer than 1 unit. 7. river-course carries a point list, and at least 2 routes cross it. 8. At least 3 stations carry class interchange, and each of them names at least 2 distinct routes in data-routes. 9. Every route carries at least 2 stations of class terminus naming it, one of them within 1.5 units of each end of its centreline. 10. The map carries at least 20 stations; every one has a usable position, names at least one route in data-routes, names only routes that exist, and sits within 1.5 units of each route it names. 11. Every route carries at least 6 stops, no two in the same place, and the longest gap between consecutive stops along it is at most 2.5 times the shortest. 12. Two centrelines never come within 12 units of each other except within 30 units of a station marked interchange. 13. The legend holds at least 4 non-empty text labels and a swatch painted in every route's centreline colour. 14. scale holds a drawn bar and a text giving a distance in km, m or mi; compass holds a drawn needle and a text label N. If the contract cannot be satisfied, return status='failure' with the precise reason rather than a partial drawing or a file that dodges the tests.
contract: Produce ONE SVG document in the `code` field, starting with <svg and ending with </svg>. The root <svg> needs xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" and a viewBox at least 600 by 400. Tag the semantic parts with these exact ids so the map is inspectable: map (the group holding the whole drawing), backdrop (the sheet rect), river (the water group), river-course (the polyline the water follows), bridges (the crossing marks), lines (the group of routes), stations (the group of station markers), labels (the station names), legend, scale, compass, masthead. Each route is a <g id="route-a">, <g id="route-b">, ... one lowercase letter each, at least four of them. Inside each, the geometry the tests read is a <polyline class="centreline"> with a numeric points= list of at least 4 points and a literal stroke="#rrggbb" unique to that route; a wider casing polyline without that class may sit behind it. Every consecutive pair of points must differ by a horizontal, a vertical or an exact 45 degree step. river-course is a <polyline> with a numeric points= list. Every station marker carries class="station" plus one of tick, interchange or terminus, and a data-routes attribute listing the letters of the routes it serves, space separated. A marker is either a <circle> with numeric cx and cy or a <line> with numeric x1, y1, x2, y2 whose midpoint is the stop; that point must lie on every route it names. No element outside the station markers may carry the class station, so the legend's symbols must use a different class name. The legend needs one swatch per route painted in that route's exact stroke colour and a text naming it. scale needs a drawn bar and a text such as "3 km". compass needs a drawn needle and a text reading N. Everything inline: no external fonts, no raster images, no scripts, no stylesheets, no network. Gradients, groups and <defs> are fine, but no transform may move a centreline, a station or the river, since the tests read raw coordinates.
